script: OpenAI just gave ChatGPT a tiny coworker with its own computer — and it doesn’t clock out. They’re called Dots. Instead of living inside one chat bubble, a Dot can connect to your apps, use its own cloud computer, and keep chewing through a multi-step job in the background. OpenAI is pitching them for real work and personal errands, with specialist Dots for companies, and teams of Dots planned later. But here’s the catch: sensitive actions can still need your approval, and right now Dots require an eligible paid ChatGPT plan, while Meta’s Muse offers a free tier. So the next AI race isn’t just who has the smartest chatbot. It’s who gets to become your always-on digital coworker. Would you give one the keys?
audience: AI-curious adults and knowledge workers deciding whether persistent agents deserve access to their apps
rationale: Propositions: b02 establishes app access; b03 locates execution on the Dot's separate computer; b04 develops an assigned job without foreground attention. Five completed failures require abandoning the Bot-operated deck family. Split connection from computation and make the original Dot token the sole causal actor. Archive the rejected concept before applying this patch; preserve the exact script and all eight locked setups. Supplied connection evidence is limited: Dd2uCwTB6II-s09 frames [834,847) show prompt placement but do not resolve transfer or submission contact. Continuing-process evidence is stronger: audiobook frames [507,559) preserve recognizable material through changing output, and Dd2UAqOvDoO-s05 frames [639,652) preserve workload identity across sampled states. Transfer those relationships only. These stills do not prove replacement contacts or playback; production BEFORE, CONTACT and AFTER remain NOT_ASSESSED until caption-free native evidence is reviewed. This patch proposes agent-assisted artwork and action contracts, not executable choreography or a quality PASS. The unused moving-repair budget remains separate.
metaphor: Unchanged worlds retain their own setup rules. Replacement relationships: The Dot token contacts a fixed app terminal; that contact changes the terminal from disconnected to connected. The Dot-controlled computer draws one identifiable job strip through a supported working aperture, exposing successive source, outline and unfinished-draft states.
